items.stem: Explain the difference between congruent and similar figures, with an example.
items.answer: Similar: same shape (proportional sides, equal angles); congruent: same shape and size. e.g. two circles of radii 2 cm and 5 cm are similar, not congruent.
items.markingKey: Key points: Similar: same shape (proportional sides, equal angles); congruent: same shape and size. e.g. two circles of radii 2 cm and 5 cm are similar, not congruent. Award 2 marks for a complete, correctly reasoned answer.

items.stem: On a map with scale 1 : 25,000, two towns are 6 cm apart. Using the idea of similar figures, find the actual distance in km.
Is a rectangle of 3 cm × 4 cm similar to a rectangle of 7.5 cm × 12 cm? Justify.
items.markingKey: All angles are 90°; compare ratios 3/7.5 = 2/5 and 4/12 = 1/3: not equal, so not similar.

items.stem: Kunal prints a photograph of size 4 cm × 6 cm and then enlarges it to 20 cm × 30 cm for a school exhibition. (i) Are the two prints similar? Why? (ii) What is the scale factor? (iii) If the original shows a tree 2.5 cm tall, how tall is it in the enlargement? (iv) Would a 20 cm × 32 cm print be similar to the original?
items.answer: (i) yes: angles 90° and sides in ratio 1 : 5 (ii) 5 (iii) 12.5 cm (iv) no, 4/20 ≠ 6/32
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.markingKey: (b) Rectangles may have different length-breadth ratios.

items.stem: Is a rectangle of 11 cm × 10 cm similar to a rectangle of 27.5 cm × 25 cm? Justify.
items.markingKey: All angles are 90°; compare ratios 11/27.5 = 2/5 and 10/25 = 2/5: equal, so similar.

items.stem: Is a rectangle of 11 cm × 12 cm similar to a rectangle of 33 cm × 36 cm? Justify.
items.markingKey: All angles are 90°; compare ratios 11/33 = 1/3 and 12/36 = 1/3: equal, so similar.

items.stem: A triangle has sides (among others) 7 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm. A similar triangle has scale factor 2. Find the side corresponding to 7 cm.

items.answer: False; e.g. isosceles triangles with vertex angles 40° and 100° have different angles.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): In △ABC, DE ∥ BC with AD = 6 cm, DB = 6 cm and AE = 12 cm; then EC = 12 cm.
Reason (R): A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC and diagonals meeting at O. Prove that AO/BO = CO/DO.
items.answer: Draw EO ∥ DC through O meeting AD at E. In △ADC, EO ∥ DC ⇒ AE/ED = AO/OC; in △DAB, EO ∥ AB ⇒ AE/ED = BO/OD; hence AO/OC = BO/OD, i.e. AO/BO = CO/DO.
items.markingKey: Construction (1), two applications of BPT (2 + 1), conclusion (1).

items.stem: In △ABC, DE ∥ BC, D on AB and E on AC. If AD = 15 cm, AB = 27 cm and AC = 27 cm, find AE.
items.markingKey: AD/AB = AE/AC (corollary of BPT) ⇒ AE = 15 × 27 / 27 = 15 cm.

items.stem: In △ABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. If AD = x, DB = x + 2, AE = x − 1 and EC = x (in cm), find x.
items.markingKey: AD/DB = AE/EC ⇒ (x)(x) = (x + 2)(x − 1); the x² terms cancel ⇒ x = 2.

items.stem: ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC; its diagonals meet at O. If AO = 24 cm, OC = 12 cm, BO = 8 cm, find OD.
items.markingKey: Draw EO ∥ AB through O; by BPT, AO/OC = BO/OD. Solve: OD = 4 cm (3 marks).

items.stem: A triangular park ABC in Mumbai has a straight walking path DE parallel to the boundary BC, with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 100 m, DB = 60 m and AC = 96 m. (i) State the theorem that relates these lengths. (ii) Find AE. (iii) Find EC. (iv) If instead D were the mid-point of AB, where would E lie?
items.answer: (i) Basic Proportionality Theorem: AD/DB = AE/EC (ii) 60 m (iii) 36 m (iv) at the mid-point of AC
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: The diagonals of a quadrilateral ABCD intersect at O such that AO/OC = BO/OD. If AO = 3x − 3, OC = x − 1, BO = x − 1 and OD = 2 (in cm), find x.
items.markingKey: (3x − 3) × 2 = (x − 1)(x − 1) ⇒ x² − 8x + 7 = 0 ⇒ x = 7; x = 1 is rejected because a length would be negative or zero.

items.stem: In △ABC, D and E are points on AB and AC such that DE ∥ BC. If AD = 7.5 cm, DB = 10 cm, EC = 4 cm, find AE.
items.markingKey: By the Basic Proportionality Theorem, AD/DB = AE/EC; substitute and solve: AE = 3 cm.

items.stem: Prove the Basic Proportionality Theorem: if a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.
items.answer: In △ABC with DE ∥ BC: ar(ADE)/ar(BDE) = AD/DB and ar(ADE)/ar(DEC) = AE/EC; ar(BDE) = ar(DEC) (same base DE, between the same parallels), so AD/DB = AE/EC.
items.markingKey: Figure and given/to prove (1), draw EM ⟂ AB, DN ⟂ AC and write the area ratios (2), equal areas of BDE and DEC (1), conclusion (1).

items.stem: The diagonals of a quadrilateral ABCD intersect at O such that AO/OC = BO/OD. If AO = 3x − 12, OC = x − 6, BO = x − 1 and OD = 2 (in cm), find x.
items.markingKey: (3x − 12) × 2 = (x − 6)(x − 1) ⇒ x² − 13x + 30 = 0 ⇒ x = 10; x = 3 is rejected because a length would be negative or zero.

items.stem: Using BPT, prove that a line drawn through the mid-point of one side of a triangle parallel to another side bisects the third side.
items.answer: In △ABC, D is the mid-point of AB and DE ∥ BC. By BPT AD/DB = AE/EC; AD = DB ⇒ AE = EC.
items.markingKey: Statement (1), BPT (2), conclusion (2).

items.stem: The diagonals of a quadrilateral ABCD intersect at O such that AO/OC = BO/OD. If AO = 2x − 6, OC = x − 3, BO = x − 3 and OD = 4 (in cm), find x.
items.markingKey: (2x − 6) × 4 = (x − 3)(x − 3) ⇒ x² − 14x + 33 = 0 ⇒ x = 11; x = 3 is rejected because a length would be negative or zero.

items.stem: D and E are points on sides PQ and PR of △PQR with PD = 5 cm, DQ = 6 cm, PE = 15 cm and ER = 18.5 cm. Is DE ∥ QR? Justify.
items.markingKey: PD/DQ = 5/6, PE/ER = 30/37; not equal, so DE is not parallel to QR.

items.stem: ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC; its diagonals meet at O. If OC = 15 cm, BO = 7 cm, OD = 5 cm, find AO.
items.markingKey: Draw EO ∥ AB through O; by BPT, AO/OC = BO/OD. Solve: AO = 21 cm (3 marks).

items.stem: A triangular park ABC in Dehradun has a straight walking path DE parallel to the boundary BC, with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 150 m, DB = 100 m and AC = 75 m. (i) State the theorem that relates these lengths. (ii) Find AE. (iii) Find EC. (iv) If instead D were the mid-point of AB, where would E lie?
items.answer: (i) Basic Proportionality Theorem: AD/DB = AE/EC (ii) 45 m (iii) 30 m (iv) at the mid-point of AC
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

Thales theorem

items.stem: The diagonals of a quadrilateral ABCD intersect at O such that AO/OC = BO/OD. If AO = 2x − 11, OC = x − 6, BO = x − 2 and OD = 3 (in cm), find x.
items.markingKey: (2x − 11) × 3 = (x − 6)(x − 2) ⇒ x² − 14x + 45 = 0 ⇒ x = 9; x = 5 is rejected because a length would be negative or zero.

items.markingKey: Key points: SAS similarity; ∠A = ∠D and ∠C = ∠F. Award 2 marks for a complete, correctly reasoned answer.

items.markingKey: AB/PQ = AC/PR = 2/5; but the included angles differ, so SAS fails.

items.stem: An architect makes a model triangle of sides 4 cm, 6 cm and 8 cm for a roof truss. The real truss has sides 1200 cm, 1800 cm and 2400 cm. (i) Find the ratio of corresponding sides. (ii) Which criterion shows the triangles are similar? (iii) Is the model triangle right-angled? Check using 4² + 6² and 8². (iv) What is the perimeter of the real truss in metres?
items.answer: (i) 1 : 300 (ii) SSS similarity (iii) 52 ≠ 64, so the largest angle is not 90° (iv) 54 m

items.stem: △ABC ~ △PQR. If ∠A = 60° and ∠C = 44°, find ∠R.
items.markingKey: Corresponding angles of similar triangles are equal; the third angle is 180° minus the other two. ∠R = 44°.

items.stem: In the figure, AB ∥ DC and the diagonals AC and BD of trapezium ABCD meet at O. Prove △OAB ~ △OCD.
items.markingKey: Key points: ∠OAB = ∠OCD and ∠OBA = ∠ODC (alternate angles), so AA similarity. Award 3 marks for a complete, correctly reasoned answer.

items.stem: In △ABC, AB = 8 cm, AC = 11 cm, ∠A = 70°. In △PQR, PQ = 16 cm, PR = 22 cm, ∠P = 60°. Are the triangles similar? If yes, state the criterion.
items.markingKey: AB/PQ = AC/PR = 1/2; but the included angles differ, so SAS fails.

items.stem: The sides of △ABC are 7 cm, 9 cm and 14 cm, and the sides of △DEF are 3.5 cm, 4.5 cm and 7 cm. Are the triangles similar? Justify.
items.markingKey: Ratios of corresponding (smallest to largest) sides: 2, 2, 2; all equal, so similar (SSS).

items.stem: In △PQR, S and T are points on QR and PR such that ∠P = ∠RTS. Show that △RPQ ~ △RTS.
items.answer: ∠R is common and ∠RPQ = ∠RTS, so △RPQ ~ △RTS by AA.

items.stem: Explain why, if △ABC ~ △DEF, then AB/DE = (AB + BC + CA)/(DE + EF + FD).
items.answer: Each side ratio equals k, so the sum of sides also has ratio k.

items.stem: A student of height 2.4 m casts a shadow 2 m long on the ground, and at the same time a water tank casts a shadow 24 m long. Find the height of the water tank.
items.markingKey: The sun's rays make equal angles, so the triangles are similar (AA): h/24 = 2.4/2 ⇒ h = 28.8 m.

items.stem: A student of height 2.4 m casts a shadow 4 m long on the ground, and at the same time a tower casts a shadow 20 m long. Find the height of the tower.
items.markingKey: The sun's rays make equal angles, so the triangles are similar (AA): h/20 = 2.4/4 ⇒ h = 12 m.

items.stem: In △ABC, ∠A = 90° and AD ⟂ BC with D on BC. If BD = 3 cm and DC = 27 cm, find AD.
items.markingKey: △ADB ~ △CDA (AA), so BD/AD = AD/DC ⇒ AD² = BD × DC = 81 ⇒ AD = 9 cm (3 marks).

items.stem: Siddharth places a small mirror on the ground 14.4 m from the foot of a building. Walking back 2.4 m from the mirror, Siddharth sees the top of the building in it. Siddharth's eyes are 1.8 m above the ground. (i) Why are the two triangles similar? (ii) Write the proportion. (iii) Find the height of the building. (iv) If Siddharth stood 0.5 m further back, would the height found change? Explain.
items.answer: (i) right angles at the feet and equal angles of incidence and reflection (AA) (ii) H/14.4 = 1.8/2.4 (iii) 10.8 m (iv) no, the building height is fixed; the mirror would have to move
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Manish, who is 90 cm tall, walks away from the base of a lamp post at 1.2 m/s. The lamp is 5.4 m above the ground. Find the length of Manish's shadow after 3 seconds.
items.markingKey: Distance from the post = 3.6 m. Similar triangles: 0.9/s = 5.4/(3.6 + s) ⇒ s = 0.9 × 3.6/(5.4 − 0.9) = 0.72 m (3 marks).

items.stem: △ABC ~ △PQR with AB = 6 cm, BC = 12 cm, CA = 14 cm and RP = 28 cm. Find PQ.
items.markingKey: CA/RP = AB/PQ ⇒ PQ = 6 × 28/14 = 12 cm.

items.stem: A vertical pole of height 1.5 m casts a shadow 1 m long on the ground, and at the same time a water tank casts a shadow 20 m long. Find the height of the water tank.

items.stem: Explain how similar triangles help find the height of a tree from its shadow without climbing it.
items.answer: Measure a stick and its shadow at the same time; the triangles are similar (AA), so tree height = stick height × tree shadow ÷ stick shadow.
items.markingKey: Key points: Measure a stick and its shadow at the same time; the triangles are similar (AA), so tree height = stick height × tree shadow ÷ stick shadow. Award 2 marks for a complete, correctly reasoned answer.

items.stem: A quadrilateral has sides (among others) 5 cm, 11 cm and 13 cm. A similar quadrilateral has scale factor 4. Find the side corresponding to 13 cm.

items.stem: Explain why SSA (two sides and a non-included angle) is not a criterion for similarity.
items.answer: Two different triangle shapes can have the same two sides and non-included angle, so the shape is not fixed.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Is a rectangle of 10 cm × 2 cm similar to a rectangle of 30 cm × 6 cm? Justify.
items.markingKey: All angles are 90°; compare ratios 10/30 = 1/3 and 2/6 = 1/3: equal, so similar.

items.stem: Explain why a square and a rhombus of the same side need not be similar.
items.answer: Sides are proportional (ratio 1) but corresponding angles need not be equal (rhombus angles may not be 90°).
items.markingKey: Key points: Sides are proportional (ratio 1) but corresponding angles need not be equal (rhombus angles may not be 90°). Award 2 marks for a complete, correctly reasoned answer.

items.stem: A pentagon has sides (among others) 4 cm, 9 cm and 12 cm. A similar pentagon has scale factor 4. Find the side corresponding to 4 cm.
items.markingKey: Corresponding sides are proportional: 4 × 4 = 16 cm.

items.stem: Diya prints a photograph of size 4 cm × 6 cm and then enlarges it to 16 cm × 24 cm for a school exhibition. (i) Are the two prints similar? Why? (ii) What is the scale factor? (iii) If the original shows a tree 2.5 cm tall, how tall is it in the enlargement? (iv) Would a 16 cm × 26 cm print be similar to the original?
items.answer: (i) yes: angles 90° and sides in ratio 1 : 4 (ii) 4 (iii) 10 cm (iv) no, 4/16 ≠ 6/26
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Explain why, unlike triangles, two quadrilaterals with equal corresponding angles need not be similar. Give an example.
items.answer: A square and a non-square rectangle have equal angles but sides not proportional.
items.markingKey: Key points: A square and a non-square rectangle have equal angles but sides not proportional. Award 2 marks for a complete, correctly reasoned answer.

items.stem: D and E are points on sides PQ and PR of △PQR with PD = 9 cm, DQ = 2 cm, PE = 13.5 cm and ER = 3.5 cm. Is DE ∥ QR? Justify.
items.markingKey: PD/DQ = 9/2, PE/ER = 27/7; not equal, so DE is not parallel to QR.

items.stem: Two congruent figures are …
items.markingKey: (c) Congruent figures have the same shape and size.
options: never similar
similar only if they are squares
always similar
similar only if they are triangles

items.stem: A student of height 6 m casts a shadow 3 m long on the ground, and at the same time a tower casts a shadow 24 m long. Find the height of the tower.
items.markingKey: The sun's rays make equal angles, so the triangles are similar (AA): h/24 = 6/3 ⇒ h = 48 m.

items.stem: Aryan, who is 180 cm tall, walks away from the base of a lamp post at 0.6 m/s. The lamp is 7.2 m above the ground. Find the length of Aryan's shadow after 3 seconds.
items.markingKey: Distance from the post = 1.8 m. Similar triangles: 1.8/s = 7.2/(1.8 + s) ⇒ s = 1.8 × 1.8/(7.2 − 1.8) = 0.6 m (3 marks).

items.stem: In △ABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. If AD = x + 3, DB = x, AE = x + 1 and EC = x − 1 (in cm), find x.
items.markingKey: AD/DB = AE/EC ⇒ (x + 3)(x − 1) = (x)(x + 1); the x² terms cancel ⇒ x = 3.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another, the triangles are similar.
Reason (R): The sum of the angles of a triangle is 180°.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Third angles equal; AA follows.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: In △ABC, ∠A = 90° and AD ⟂ BC with D on BC. If BD = 75 cm and DC = 48 cm, find AD.
items.markingKey: △ADB ~ △CDA (AA), so BD/AD = AD/DC ⇒ AD² = BD × DC = 3600 ⇒ AD = 60 cm (3 marks).

items.stem: In △ABC and △PQR, ∠A = ∠P, ∠B = ∠Q and ∠C = ∠R. Which criterion shows that △ABC ~ △PQR?
items.markingKey: (b) Match the given equal angles or proportional sides to the criterion.
options: RHS congruence
AAA similarity
SSS similarity
SAS similarity

items.stem: The diagonals of a quadrilateral ABCD intersect at O such that AO/OC = BO/OD. If AO = 3x − 9, OC = x − 6, BO = x − 3 and OD = 2 (in cm), find x.
items.markingKey: (3x − 9) × 2 = (x − 6)(x − 3) ⇒ x² − 15x + 36 = 0 ⇒ x = 12; x = 3 is rejected because a length would be negative or zero.

items.stem: Is a rectangle of 6 cm × 10 cm similar to a rectangle of 9 cm × 15 cm? Justify.
items.markingKey: All angles are 90°; compare ratios 6/9 = 2/3 and 10/15 = 2/3: equal, so similar.

items.stem: In △ABC, DE ∥ BC, D on AB and E on AC. If AD = 12 cm, AB = 21 cm and AC = 7 cm, find AE.
items.markingKey: AD/AB = AE/AC (corollary of BPT) ⇒ AE = 12 × 7 / 21 = 4 cm.

items.stem: △ABC ~ △PQR. If ∠A = 53° and ∠B = 60°, find ∠P.
items.markingKey: Corresponding angles of similar triangles are equal; the third angle is 180° minus the other two. ∠P = 53°.

items.stem: Aditya places a small mirror on the ground 30 m from the foot of a building. Walking back 2 m from the mirror, Aditya sees the top of the building in it. Aditya's eyes are 1.6 m above the ground. (i) Why are the two triangles similar? (ii) Write the proportion. (iii) Find the height of the building. (iv) If Aditya stood 0.5 m further back, would the height found change? Explain.
items.answer: (i) right angles at the feet and equal angles of incidence and reflection (AA) (ii) H/30 = 1.6/2 (iii) 24 m (iv) no, the building height is fixed; the mirror would have to move
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Is a rectangle of 4 cm × 9 cm similar to a rectangle of 10 cm × 24.5 cm? Justify.
items.markingKey: All angles are 90°; compare ratios 4/10 = 2/5 and 9/24.5 = 18/49: not equal, so not similar.

items.stem: Explain why all circles are similar but not all ellipses-like ovals or rectangles are.
items.answer: A circle is fixed by its radius alone, so any circle is a scaled copy of another; rectangles need the same length-to-breadth ratio.
items.markingKey: Key points: A circle is fixed by its radius alone, so any circle is a scaled copy of another; rectangles need the same length-to-breadth ratio. Award 2 marks for a complete, correctly reasoned answer.
